Video 4: Must have even more extreme edits applied in order to not be picked up as a duplicate against 1, 2 and 3
So you can see that very quickly, the more times you try to repurpose 1 piece of content, the more extreme you must be with your edits, which diminishes the quality of your content to the point that you are better off just getting new content.
Meta also does make some exceptions for example on Memes, News and things like podcasts, but this is done by Machine Learning to understand if some level of duplication should be allowed on the video and we haven't got any strategies around manipulating this."

We are solving this problem in a few ways
Editing more than 50% of the video, we can do this via caption overlays (will go more into this in video)
Sourcing content from TikTok models that aren't posting on TikTok that way we can faceswap, post the content and it's 100% unique
Green Screen effects and changing the background to a screenshot/replying to guys comment on tiktok etc.
Photo strategies (video coming on this too)
Recording long form content of the model performing repetitive activities (yoga, walking, cooking) we can record for 1 hour, cut that up into 5-7 clips automatically and you basically generate 600 unique videos from one hours worth of content.
Having models perform trends that are very repeatable and fast to perform, flashing being a good example where a model can quickly make 80 - 120 reels in a day
If you then start to combine a few of these strategies above, for example, faceswap + text overlay of say 20% of the video + zoom and rotate then the combination of these can lead to a video being treated as unique but you are treading a fine line and we prefer the above strategies.
In terms of repurposing of content, the other major problem is that for each variation you have to make things more and more extreme on each variation.
So an example would be the following:
Video 1: Original
Video 2: Rotation 10% + zoom
Video 3: Must be at least 20% rotation otherwise it will be detected as a duplicate against video 2

"Also, btw. The update thingy is not bullshit. You guys are just not keeping up. Nat Aston talked about it too
Image
Basically attached is a screenshot officially released by Meta of the types of content they are able to detect duplicates on. You can see that a full rotation and 50% crop are easily detected by them.
Basically this means that most of the 'unique edits' people are making are actually detectable.
There's some strange things going on at the moment, for example some people have been hit massively by IG updates, where as others not reporting anything and even boasting that they are posting the same content again and again without getting flagged - so there's mixed reports.
Our assumption as that duplicate detection hasn't been rolled out internationally, perhaps they are testing in certain areas first, perhaps due to limited capacity of GPU infrastructure to analyse every single real frame by frame and run comparisons to detect duplicates (Zuckerberg mentioned something along these lines in a podcast before that their GPU orders kept getting delayed.)
Anyway, the one thing we are 100% sure of is that it's coming and will be rolled out for everyone in the near future. Meta also has insane budget and the best engineers in the world to detect duplicates, so a 3% rotation and brightness change is easily picked up by them, face-swapping and everyone else is also detected.
